title: 2010 HMMT February General Round 1 Problem 1
statement:
Suppose that \(x\) and \(y\) are positive reals such that

\[x-y^{2}=3, \quad x^{2}+y^{4}=13\]

Find \(x\).

solutions.text: \(\frac{3+\sqrt{17}}{2}\) Squaring both sides of \(x-y^{2}=3\) gives \(x^{2}+y^{4}-2 x y^{2}=9\). Subtract this equation from twice the second given to get \(x^{2}+2 x y^{2}+y^{4}=17 \Longrightarrow x+y^{2}= \pm 17\). Combining this equation with the first given, we see that \(x=\frac{3 \pm \sqrt{17}}{2}\). Since \(x\) is a positive real, \(x\) must be \(\frac{3+\sqrt{17}}{2}\).
